Package io.webagent4j.crawler.api

Record Class CrawlStatistics

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
io.webagent4j.crawler.api.CrawlStatistics
Record Components:
discoveredUrls - distinct normalized URLs admitted into navigation/frontier discovery during this crawl - every seed and every HTML link accepted by the scope/depth/dedup checks that gate frontier entry. A redirect target is never a discovered URL, only a fetched one; see fetchedUrls(). Includes URLs enqueued but never actually fetched because maxPages was reached first
fetchedUrls - distinct normalized URLs for which at least one real HTTP request was actually started - every redirect hop actually followed counts as its own fetched URL, in addition to each task's own starting URL; retries of the same URL never count more than once. This is exactly the quantity CrawlRequest.maxPages() bounds, claimed immediately before every one of these requests, including a redirect hop - never discovered only after the request was already sent
successfulPages - number of CrawlResult.pages() entries; always equal to pages.size()
failedUrls - number of CrawlResult.failures() entries; always equal to failures.size(). This is a count of crawl-task outcomes that ended in failure, not of network requests that failed - a failure can be recorded for a URL that was never actually fetched (see CrawlFailureType.CRAWL_LIMIT_REACHED, CrawlFailureType.ALREADY_FETCHED), so this value must never be assumed derivable from fetchedUrls
rejectedUrls - discovered candidate links that scope policy, depth, URL filters, or the deduplicator rejected before ever entering the frontier
redirects - total redirect hops actually followed across every fetch attempt
duplicateUrls - discovery attempts suppressed because the normalized URL was already claimed by the frontier/discovery deduplicator - a separate concept from a redirect converging onto an already-fetched identity, which is instead a CrawlFailureType.ALREADY_FETCHED CrawlFailure and does not affect this counter
totalBytes - sum of responseBytes across every HTTP response that was read in full (successful or a terminal HTTP status), across every retry and every redirect hop. A response aborted for exceeding CrawlRequest.maxResponseBytes() contributes nothing to this total: the byte count at the moment of abortion is not tracked
maxDepthReached - the greatest crawl-task depth among tasks for which at least one real HTTP request was actually started - a task whose fetch identity claim failed before any request was sent (maxPages exhausted, or the identity already fetched) never contributes here, even though it may still produce a CrawlFailure. Redirect hops followed while resolving a task never change that task's depth
public record CrawlStatistics(int discoveredUrls, int fetchedUrls, int successfulPages, int failedUrls, int rejectedUrls, int redirects, int duplicateUrls, long totalBytes, int maxDepthReached) extends Record
Immutable crawl-wide counters. Every field has one precise, independent definition. Deliberately no general mathematical relationship is asserted between fetchedUrls(), successfulPages(), and failedUrls(): a CrawlFailure can be recorded for a URL that was never actually requested - CrawlFailureType.CRAWL_LIMIT_REACHED and CrawlFailureType.ALREADY_FETCHED both add an entry to CrawlResult.failures() (and so to failedUrls) without adding a new fetch identity (so without increasing fetchedUrls) - so failedUrls is never derivable from fetchedUrls, in either direction, in general.
